extracted.intended_audience: researchers and potential DARPA proposers (academia, industry, government), program managers, and contractors
extracted.subtask_description: Agency-level guidance and evaluative criteria for DARPA research programs, including the requirement to answer the Heilmeier Catechism, policies on fundamental research and dissemination, ELSI engagement, and the preferred style of high-risk/high-reward, cross-disciplinary work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heilmeier Catechism
rubrics_metrics.description: Every program begins by answering eight questions – a rubric known as the Heilmeier Catechism – to determine whether the risk is worth taking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach empowers DARPA to respond to constant change in the national security landscape while simultaneously capitalizing on – and driving – emergent advancements in science and technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental research openness
rubrics_metrics.description: Our fundamental research awards are free from publication restrictions, export controls, and citizenship requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We also place no restrictions on unclassified research assigned to subcontractors if the prime contractor and research performer determine the activity to be fundamental research, subject to certification by the contracting component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation declaration of research classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Each solicitation and award announcement states explicitly whether the activity constitutes fundamental research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposers and awardees should consult solicitation/award language to determine whether an activity is designated as fundamental research and therefore free from certain restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security-based dissemination restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrictions are applied when necessary to safeguard national security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such restrictions include preventing the disclosure of the performance characteristics of military systems as well as manufacturing technologies that are unique and critical to defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: ELSI (Ethical, Legal, and Societal Implications) engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Program managers and research performers actively engage potential end users and the public during the program development process to consider ethical, legal, and societal implications of emerging technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DARPA leaders and staff are supported by an ELSI Visiting Scholar to ensure that all implications are considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-risk, high-reward focus
rubrics_metrics.description: DARPA's focus is on high-risk, high-reward R&D to maintain a technological advantage for the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agency's approach rewards visionary thinking, ambitious risk-taking, and cross-disciplinary collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program structure: finite-duration with transition emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Research programs are finite in duration but are designed to drive revolutionary advancements that create lasting change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs are structured to include efforts such as challenges, seedlings, explorations, initiatives, and technology transition activities to move innovations toward impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diverse engagement and participation mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Opportunities to engage with DARPA include R&D programs and efforts, challenge competitions, and technology transition efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DARPA seeks to bring together scientists, engineers, and tinkerers across the innovation ecosystem and to engage the best ideas across specialties, communities, and perspectives (e.g., via DARPAConnect).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for cross-disciplinary leadership and experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Program managers are expected to be visionary leaders whose experience spans industry, government, and academia and who can conceive, plan, and oversee high-risk R&D efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program leadership and teams should enable cross-disciplinary collaboration to pursue ambitious, transformative technical goals.
